subject: OrbitCloud — request for maintenance scoping & probe evidence (partial degradation)
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@orbitcloud.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: orbit-contracts@orbitcloud.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observed partial degradation 2027-07-20 — request to scope exclusion

Soojin,

We saw a persistent latency spike across a subset of requests to your hosted inference endpoint (model: redwood-ff-large) between 2027-07-20T14:03:00Z and 2027-07-20T14:57:00Z. Our synthetic probes (IDs included in the attached logs) indicate a progressive increase in tail latency that coincides with a scheduled maintenance window on our CDN provider (EdgeWave), which they say affected a small fanout in our POPs.

Per section 3.2 of our SLA, we believe this qualifies as a third-party maintenance event that should be considered for exclusion when calculating uptime. We are opening this with our procurement team (cc'd) and have attached the probe logs and a short packet capture for your SREs to review.

Request: can you confirm whether Redwood's telemetry shows a workload-level prefix/KV cache invalidation or backend failover during the same window? If so, we'd like you to exclude the EdgeWave maintenance window from the numerator for the uptime calculation and propose apportionment if Redwood infrastructure contributed in any measurable way.

Attachments: orbit_uplink_log_2027-07-20.zip (probe logs, packet snips)

Thanks — looking to keep this tidy for our finance/procurement review.

— Sam Patel
Director, Platform Engineering
OrbitCloud
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@orbitcloud.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, orbit-contracts@orbitcloud.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed partial degradation 2027-07-20 — request to scope exclusion

Thanks Sam — appreciate the fast heads-up and the logs. We have two simultaneous asks so I want to be explicit about next steps: 1) I will loop in SRE (karthik) to correlate Redwood traces with your probe timestamps; 2) Ben and Marissa will help coordinate the apportionment and any interim credit conversation with contracts.

Could you confirm the exact UTC start/end you want excluded (the ZIP has multiple probe hits)? Also, please point us at the ORBIT ticket or maintenance advisory from EdgeWave so we can cross-check the overlap. If you prefer, we can set a short call tomorrow to walk telemetry together.

I'll ask SRE to produce a preliminary apportionment calculation by EOD Thursday (2027-07-22). If that works for you, we'll treat the investigation as a harmonized ticket and keep procurement in the loop.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Account Lead — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 17:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OrbitCloud maintenance exclusion request — initial proposal

Looping in quick thoughts — thanks for flagging. Two options for a fast path:

- Option A (conservative): Treat the EdgeWave maintenance window as external; exclude the exact UTC window from uptime numerator if our traces show no backend failover or degraded serving instances.
- Option B (shared): If our KV/prefix cache invalidation or a short-lived failover amplified the impact, propose an apportionment (we split the impacted minutes proportionally to measured error/latency contribution).

Karthik: I'm attaching a brief trace snippet I pulled from the serving mesh (redwood_trace_snippet_0720.txt). Please correlate the request IDs with the probe list Sam sent and confirm whether any model-host-level failovers or notable KV cache churn happened.

I'll draft suggested language for contracts if we land on apportionment.

— Ben
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@orbitcloud.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: orbit-contracts@orbitcloud.com, ops@orbitcloud.com
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observed partial degradation 2027-07-20 — request to scope exclusion

Soojin,

Thanks — confirming the window we'd like considered is 2027-07-20T14:00:00Z to 2027-07-20T15:00:00Z. EdgeWave posted a planned maintenance advisory that started at 2027-07-20T13:50:00Z (we saw initial probe jitter) and closed at 2027-07-20T16:05:00Z; the most notable tail latency was between 14:03–14:57 UTC.

Drive link to our ticket and the advisory: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bOrbitCloudEvidence (includes the advisory PDF, probe IDs, and a short video of synthetic probe graphs).

Orbit's procurement note: we will consider an exclusion if Redwood confirms no internal failover contributed. If Redwood finds a minor contribution we will accept apportionment. Orbit is submitting a formal credit request for ~15% of July usage tied to that hour; we expect the apportionment/calculation to be the basis for any credit.

Let me know if you want a quick conference (we have a 30-min slot 2027-07-22T15:00Z).

— Sam
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@orbitcloud.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, orbit-contracts@orbitcloud.com
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed partial degradation 2027-07-20 — investigation plan and deliverables

Sam — thanks for the confirmation and the Drive bundle. Quick summary of our plan / timeline so procurement and ops have a single point of truth: 

1) Karthik (SRE) will run a probe correlation and produce a minute-by-minute apportionment worksheet showing per-minute request counts, error rate delta, and whether any host-level failover or cache invalidation was observed. Deliverable: sla_calc_workbook.xlsx (prelim) by 2027-07-22 EOD PST.

2) If Karthik's analysis shows zero measurable failover or serving-layer contribution, Redwood will propose excluding the 14:00–15:00 UTC slot from the uptime numerator. If there is measurable contribution we will propose a split apportionment and provide the workings.

3) Ben/Marissa will draft a one-page redline-ready confirmation for Orbit's procurement describing the exclusion/apportionment result and the proposed credit (if any).

4) Interim: We'll place a credit-hold flag on the account so billing doesn't auto-close until the investigation completes. If Orbit would prefer immediate provisional credit instead of a hold, say so and we'll route through finance.

5) Call: we can take the 2027-07-22 15:00Z slot if that's still good — propose we use it only if the parties want to walk the workbook live.

Karthik — prioritizing this; please ping if you need additional logs or the probe IDs from the Orbit zip.

I'll follow up with the workbook when it lands and mark the ticket with the HubSpot deal.

Best,

Soojin
Account Lead — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
